headline: Indian markets crash as Sensex tumbles 1,100 points amid US-Iran tensions and rising crude oil prices

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Escalating US-Iran conflict after Trump rejected a peace proposal
Sharp spike in global crude oil prices impacting sentiment
Significant FII outflows and bets on potential interest rate hikes
Global sell-off in commodities with gold and silver plunging up to 3%
whatHappening: Sensex plunged over 1,100 points while Nifty 50 dropped below the 22,800 level
Investors lost approximately Rs 6 lakh crore in market wealth during the session
Indian shares reached a near six-month low due to geopolitical deadlocks
The Income Tax department extended corporate tax audit and ITR filing deadlines by three weeks
summary: The Indian stock market witnessed a massive sell-off on Monday, with the Sensex crashing 1,100 points and Nifty falling below 22,800. Geopolitical tensions between the US and Iran, coupled with surging crude oil prices and FII outflows, triggered a 'Monday mayhem' that wiped out Rs 6 lakh crore in investor wealth. Amid the broader decline, Morepen Laboratories hit a milestone by filing its first US ANDA for sitagliptin tablets.
